{"intent":"answer","response":"Here’s a concise, current FAFSA checklist and timeline tailored to your constraint (private caregiving; ~2 hours/week). I’m assuming you’re filing the 2026–27 FAFSA. If you meant a different aid year, tell me which one and I’ll swap the tax year, dates, and links.

What “requirements” means now
- Basic eligibility (unchanged essentials):
  - U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; valid SSN for the student (certain territorial exceptions exist).  
  - Enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an eligible program; satisfactory academic progress per school policy.  
  - No default on federal student loans; no owed federal grant overpayment.  
  - Selective Service registration and drug‑conviction questions no longer affect aid eligibility.  
- FAFSA contributors and consent (critical):
  - All required “contributors” must each have an FSA ID and give consent for IRS Direct Data Exchange (DDX), or an SAI won’t be calculated.  
  - Contributors are: the student; the student’s spouse (if married); parent(s) if the student is dependent (parental set depends on who provided more support in the last 12 months; if remarried, include stepparent).  
  - Contributors without an SSN can still create an FSA ID (identity verification alternatives are provided).  
- What year’s income is used (2026–27):
  - 2024 federal tax year via IRS DDX (prior‑prior year).  
  - Manual entry is limited; DDX consent is the default path.  
- Dependency rules (high‑impact):
  - Independent if any apply: born before Jan 1, 2003; married; veteran/active duty; graduate/professional student; has dependents they support; emancipated, in legal guardianship, unaccompanied homeless youth, or at risk of homelessness. Otherwise generally dependent and must include parent info.  
- Outcome metric:
  - FAFSA now produces a Student Aid Index (SAI) instead of EFC; SAI can be negative and is how schools assess need.  

Key dates for 2026–27 FAFSA
- Opening: expected October 1, 2025 (subject to Federal Student Aid confirmation; some years have shifted).  
- Federal deadline: June 30, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Central Time.  
- Correction deadline: mid‑September 2027 (FSA posts exact date each cycle).  
- State and school deadlines vary and are often earlier—file as soon as practical for priority aid.  

What you’ll need to complete it
- For each contributor: FSA ID (set up or confirm access), full legal name, DOB, SSN (if available) or alternative verification, email/phone.  
- 2024 tax situation: filing status and whether a 2024 return was filed; DDX consent lets FSA pull income data.  
- Student’s driver’s license (optional), alien registration number if applicable, list of target schools to receive the FAFSA.  
- Household and college plans: number in household; number in college (reported but no longer divides SAI).  

Two-hours‑per‑week plan around your caregiving constraint
- Week 1 (30–45 min): Confirm which aid year you’re filing (likely 2026–27). Make/verify your FSA ID; identify all required contributors and have them create/verify theirs.  
- Week 1 (30–45 min): Skim dependency questions to confirm whether parent info is required; pick the right parent(s) per support rule.  
- Week 2 (30–45 min): Line up target schools (you can add more later). Check each school and your state’s earlier priority deadlines.  
- Week 2 (30–45 min): Ensure each contributor is ready to give DDX consent. If any contributor lacks an SSN, complete FSA ID identity verification early.  
- Filing window: Submit within your first free hour after FAFSA opens; aim for within the first 2–3 weeks for best school/state aid consideration.  

Common snags to avoid
- A required contributor doesn’t create an FSA ID or won’t give IRS DDX consent (no SAI).

{"intent":"answer","response":"Here’s a concise, current FAFSA checklist and timeline tailored to your constraint (private caregiving; ~2 hours/week). I’m assuming you’re filing the 2026–27 FAFSA. If you meant a different aid year, tell me which one and I’ll swap the tax year, dates, and links.

What “requirements” means now
- Basic eligibility (unchanged essentials):
  - U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; valid SSN for the student (certain territorial exceptions exist).  
  - Enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an eligible program; satisfactory academic progress per school policy.  
  - No default on federal student loans; no owed federal grant overpayment.  
  - Selective Service registration and drug‑conviction questions no longer affect aid eligibility.  
- FAFSA contributors and consent (critical):
  - All required “contributors” must each have an FSA ID and give consent for IRS Direct Data Exchange (DDX), or an SAI won’t be calculated.  
  - Contributors are: the student; the student’s spouse (if married); parent(s) if the student is dependent (parental set depends on who provided more support in the last 12 months; if remarried, include stepparent).  
  - Contributors without an SSN can still create an FSA ID (identity verification alternatives are provided).  
- What year’s income is used (2026–27):
  - 2024 federal tax year via IRS DDX (prior‑prior year).  
  - Manual entry is limited; DDX consent is the default path.  
- Dependency rules (high‑impact):
  - Independent if any apply: born before Jan 1, 2003; married; veteran/active duty; graduate/professional student; has dependents they support; emancipated, in legal guardianship, unaccompanied homeless youth, or at risk of homelessness. Otherwise generally dependent and must include parent info.  
- Outcome metric:
  - FAFSA now produces a Student Aid Index (SAI) instead of EFC; SAI can be negative and is how schools assess need.  

Key dates for 2026–27 FAFSA
- Opening: expected October 1, 2025 (subject to Federal Student Aid confirmation; some years have shifted).  
- Federal deadline: June 30, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Central Time.  
- Correction deadline: mid‑September 2027 (FSA posts exact date each cycle).  
- State and school deadlines vary and are often earlier—file as soon as practical for priority aid.  

What you’ll need to complete it
- For each contributor: FSA ID (set up or confirm access), full legal name, DOB, SSN (if available) or alternative verification, email/phone.  
- 2024 tax situation: filing status and whether a 2024 return was filed; DDX consent lets FSA pull income data.  
- Student’s driver’s license (optional), alien registration number if applicable, list of target schools to receive the FAFSA.  
- Household and college plans: number in household; number in college (reported but no longer divides SAI).  

Two-hours‑per‑week plan around your caregiving constraint
- Week 1 (30–45 min): Confirm which aid year you’re filing (likely 2026–27). Make/verify your FSA ID; identify all required contributors and have them create/verify theirs.  
- Week 1 (30–45 min): Skim dependency questions to confirm whether parent info is required; pick the right parent(s) per support rule.  
- Week 2 (30–45 min): Line up target schools (you can add more later). Check each school and your state’s earlier priority deadlines.  
- Week 2 (30–45 min): Ensure each contributor is ready to give DDX consent. If any contributor lacks an SSN, complete FSA ID identity verification early.  
- Filing window: Submit within your first free hour after FAFSA opens; aim for within the first 2–3 weeks for best school/state aid consideration.  

Common snags to avoid
- A required contributor doesn’t create an FSA ID or won’t give IRS DDX consent (no SAI).  
- Choosing the wrong parent for a dependent student (use the 12‑month financial support rule; if exactly equal, use the higher‑income parent).  
- Name/SSN/DOB mismatches with Social Security Administration records.
